token: A chunk of text, often a piece of a word, that has its own id number. Language models read and write tokens, not letters.
tokenizer: The tool that chops text into tokens and swaps each one for its id, and turns ids back into text. Its dictionary is built before training and never changes.
vocabulary: The full list of tokens a model knows, each with its own id. This book mostly calls it the dictionary.
byte-pair encoding: A counting recipe for building a token dictionary: start from single characters and keep gluing together whichever pair of neighbors appears most often.
BPE: Short for byte-pair encoding: build a token dictionary by repeatedly gluing together the most common pair of neighbors.
byte: The unit a computer stores text in: a number from 0 to 255. A plain English letter is one byte; most emoji take four.
embedding table: A grid of learned numbers with one row for every token in the dictionary. A token's id says which row to read.
embedding: The row of learned numbers that a token id looks up. The id is only a row number; the meaning is in the row.
context window: The most tokens a model can read at one time. Anything that does not fit in it, the model cannot see.
special token: A token that stands for a signal instead of text, such as end-of-text or the start of a speaker's turn.
end-of-text: A special token that marks where a document stops. When a chatbot picks it, the reply is finished.
